architecture.mechanism: Axle torque rate limits and filters applied in a hybrid control strategy to manage acceleration and jerk, keeping jerk contributions of the hybrid powertrain below a defined tolerable limit.
architecture.intervention: Add axle torque rate-limit and filtering logic to the 2021 Toyota RAV4 powertrain control module so that commanded propulsion torque during accelerator pedal changes is slew-rate limited and low-pass filtered before being sent to the engine/transmission torque actuators, coordinated with battery SOC management to preserve normal performance and emissions.
architecture.expected_effect: Jerking during acceleration is reduced by smoothing torque transitions at the wheels, while overall powertrain performance and emissions compliance are maintained because the filtering only modifies transient torque requests, not steady-state operating points.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument the vehicle with a wheel-speed sensor and longitudinal accelerometer; perform repeated tip-in/tip-out accelerations on a flat road at 20–80 km/h and measure resulting axle torque derivative and vehicle jerk; compare against the stock ECU and a calibrated threshold (e.g., 10 m/s^3). If mean and peak jerk are not statistically reduced versus stock without degrading 0–60 km/h time or tailpipe emissions on the FTP/US06 cycles, the mechanism is falsified.
